features.name: Live fixtures & scores
features.description: The board auto-populates with the real World Cup schedule and live scores, pulled from ESPN, with each match bucketed into its phase (Group, R32, R16, QF, SF, Final).
features.notes: ESPN scoreboard, no API key; UTC kickoffs shifted -8h so games bucket on the real match day

features.name: 12-group standings
features.description: Real group tables (played, W/D/L, GF/GA/GD, points) straight from ESPN, with a fallback that computes standings from any scores you enter manually.
features.notes: ESPN standings endpoint + local computeStandings() from entered scores

features.name: Real bracket as teams qualify
features.description: The knockout bracket fills with real teams as they qualify, showing TBD placeholders until then.
features.notes: aReal/bReal flags distinguish real teams from 'Winner of…' placeholders

features.name: Auto-refresh
features.description: Live data refreshes on a schedule in the background and the page re-polls so the board stays current without a manual reload.
features.notes: Proxy scheduler every refresh_minutes (15); page polls /snapshot every 60s

features.name: Player power scores
features.description: Every player gets a transparent 0-100 Player Power Score. By default this comes from real EA FC 26 player ratings mapped to national teams — a realistic stand-in while the 2026 squads aren't published yet.
features.notes: player_source=fifa (EA FC 26 CSV, free, no key); api-football and SAMPLE are alternatives

features.name: Team squad strength
features.description: Player scores roll up into a Squad Strength Score per team using a projected best XI, a star bonus, and a bench-depth term — so one elite player and squad depth both count.
features.notes: Spine-weighted projected XI (1 GK / 4 DEF / 3 MID / 3 ATT) + star non-linearity + bench depth

features.name: Honest data labelling
features.description: When real stats aren't available the app clearly labels players as SAMPLE rather than pretending the numbers are live.
features.notes: SAMPLE badge preserved even on warm restart; source string shown in the status line

features.name: Deep per-player stats (optional)
features.description: With a free API-Football key the scoring can use real match stats (goals, passes, tackles, etc.) for richer scores.
features.notes: Built; key optional; 2026 squads return 0 players this far out — set season 2022 to demo

features.name: Per-phase betting window
features.description: For each tournament phase the app shows the survive-to-title probability, the payout multiple, and a value score, highlighting which round is the structural sweet spot (R16/QF).
features.notes: winProb=p^rounds; payout=1/(winProb+fee); value=info×min(1,(1/winProb−1)/5)

features.name: Model-driven win probability
features.description: The per-match win probability marries squad strength with the team's actual tournament form, shifting weight toward real results as games are played.
features.notes: w=gp/(gp+3); combined=w·TFS+(1−w)·SSS; falls back to form-only with no squad model

features.name: Pick a candidate team
features.description: Choose a real team and the window recomputes around its strength and form, or enter a base probability manually.
features.notes: Team selector from real fixtures; useModel toggle; manual p nudged by form factor

features.name: Always-visible disclaimer
features.description: A prominent disclaimer keeps it clear that this is a heuristic, betting is high variance, and nothing is guaranteed profitable.
features.notes: DISCLAIMER surfaced in every proxy payload and on the page

features.name: Live market odds
features.description: Pulls live World Cup market prices from Kalshi's public API and shows implied probabilities and payouts next to the model.
features.notes: Server-side fetch (no CORS); self-heals by auto-discovering the live series. Kalshi has no WC markets listed yet — they open near the tournament

features.name: Manual odds paste
features.description: If a live feed isn't available you can paste Kalshi market JSON by hand and the app parses it into the same table.
features.notes: parseKalshi(); works even from file://

features.name: Model-vs-market edge
features.description: Compares the model's probability against the market's implied probability so you can see where the model disagrees with the crowd.
features.notes: marketEdges(); tolerant team-name matching across FIFA/ESPN/Kalshi spellings

features.name: "The Quant" chat
features.description: An AI analyst answers questions strictly from your live panels — standings, squad scores, the betting window, Kalshi — in expected-value and edge terms, and refuses to invent outside facts.
features.notes: Grounded system prompt + JSON snapshot of the panels; audited by audit_ai.py

features.name: Choose your AI engine
features.description: Use a free local AI (Ollama) or any major cloud provider — OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Azure, or a custom endpoint.
features.notes: Provider chosen in Settings; keys stay in the browser's localStorage

features.name: Free shared AI (no setup)
features.description: Out of the box the AI works with no key: the proxy holds a shared OpenRouter key server-side and falls back through free models if one is busy.
features.notes: OpenRouter key shared from C:\QI\maia.db; proxied so the browser never sees it; free-model fallback chain

features.name: Shared-AI access code
features.description: When shared over the public tunnel, the AI can be gated by an access code; change the code and stale users are instantly locked out with a friendly 'set up your own AI' message.
features.notes: Only tunnel traffic is gated (Cloudflare headers); local/exe use is never gated

features.name: Dynamic workspace
features.description: Panes can be resized, hidden, reordered by drag, and popped out into their own windows; the layout is remembered between sessions.
features.notes: Layout persisted to localStorage; pop-out bridge re-wires handlers

features.name: Runs from disk or a server
features.description: Open the HTML directly, or run the proxy and use it at localhost — the proxy serves the page same-origin so AI and live data work without CORS issues.
features.notes: Proxy GET / serves WC2026.html

features.name: Portable desktop app
features.description: Packages into a single self-contained app that opens in its own native window and carries the data proxy inside it — share it with a friend, no install needed.
features.notes: PyInstaller windowed (pywebview) + onedir builds; OS-aware output; key-sanitized bundled config

features.name: Cross-OS builds
features.description: Continuous integration builds the app for Windows, macOS, and Linux automatically.
features.notes: .github/workflows/build.yml — one binary per OS uploaded as artifacts

features.name: Shared OpenRouter key
features.description: Reuses the one OpenRouter key the ecosystem already has (from Maia), so there's no separate key to manage.
features.notes: Reads system.openrouter_api_key from C:\QI\maia.db, like MapSnap

features.name: Registered service + public tunnel
features.description: Runs as a managed Windows service and is reachable on a stable public web address through the ecosystem's tunnel system.
features.notes: QI_GamezProxy (NSSM) + QI_GamezTunnel → gamez.quiddityinnovations.com

features.name: Registry-governed ports
features.description: Uses its allocated port block from the QI ecosystem registry rather than a random port.
features.notes: Block 8710-8719; proxy on 8710

features.name: QI Brain logging
features.description: Register Gamez sessions and decisions in the QI Brain for cross-project memory.
features.notes: Not yet wired
